title: Fly nerve-cord wiring to motor neurons predicted wing-versus-leg activation behaviour of 19-20 hemilineages only as well as neuropil location; it did not predict take-off or leg posture direction
abstract: Question: does synapse-level wiring from fly ventral nerve cord hemilineages to motor-neuron pools predict the behaviour that activation of each hemilineage causes, and does it add to the neuropil location of its output? Data: the male adult nerve cord connectome MANC v1.0 (one fly) and two activation data sets from other flies: Harris et al. 2015 (19 hemilineage groups, decapitated flies, six behaviours; bar heights digitised from Figure 9A) and Gonzalez-Segarra et al. 2025 (20 split-GAL4 lines, text coded before analysis). Method: input-normalised flow from all neurons of a hemilineage to leg, wing power, wing steering, jump (TTM), haltere, neck and abdominal motor neurons over 1 to 4 synapse steps; neuropil and ROI-preserving controls; tests written before computation. Results: the wing-versus-leg wiring contrast predicted the behaviour contrast (Spearman rho 0.71, p 0.0004) and separated wing from leg lines in the second set (AUC 0.93), but the neuropil contrast gave the same values (rho 0.71, AUC 0.95; the two predictors had rho 0.98). Wiring added no gain after neuropil (partial rho 0.12, p 0.32). Targeting beyond the ROI expectation gave weak support in both sets (AUC 0.74, p 0.053; rho 0.33, p 0.083). Wiring did not predict wing buzz versus wave (rho -0.18), take-off (rho -0.12; AUC 0.59), or, with signed transmitters, leg extension versus flexion (AUC 0.37). Inhibitory hemilineages that mostly contact flexor motor neurons caused flexion. Exploratory: the unsigned direct extensor fraction went with extension (AUC 0.80, p 0.063). Limitations: small samples, digitised and qualitative phenotypes, different flies, sexes and drivers, a linear influence model, predicted transmitters, uncorrected p values. Code, aggregate tables, figures and hashes are included; MANC files stay external.

display.caption: Harris et al. 2015 groups (n = 19). Left: wing-versus-leg wiring contrast from MANC against the behaviour contrast. Middle: neuropil output contrast against the same behaviour contrast. Right: the two predictors are almost the same (rho 0.98).

Gonzalez-Segarra et al. 2025 lines (n = 20). Wiring and neuropil contrasts separate wing from leg-only lines equally well; targeting beyond the ROI expectation is weak; TTM (jump) motor-neuron share does not identify take-off lines.

Leg posture lines (n = 11). Right: the pre-specified signed extensor-minus-flexor drive does not predict extension versus flexion. Left: the exploratory unsigned direct extensor fraction does (AUC 0.80, p 0.063). Asterisk: mainly GABA or glutamate hemilineage.
